chapter: Stuff Smith Trio and New York
title: Stuff Smith's eccentricities, the union and his breakdown
summary: Stories of Stuff driving to Buffalo to see his wife, the union taking charge of salaries, and his breakdown without damage to his playing.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Had you gone to hear Stuff when John played with Stuff, before you joined the group, or --
Uh-uh.
You hadn't hear them before.
I never -- I heard him on the air. You know, Stuff had a good thing going when he was with Jonah Jones. You know.
Uh-huh.

They used to play hotels and things, you know. Cozy Cole, had some good guys in the group. Ben Webster was in his group. Clyde Hart. These were all fine musicians, you know. But Stuff had his funny ways, you know. He was a good guy, but he was just a little crazy in the head a little bit.
Like how? What was he like? I've met him, but I never really knew him.
Well, I'll give you one story. He was

working out here when the band was -- he had six pieces at that time. And the guys used to drive to work, and they would pick up -- you know, one guy would pick everybody up, you know? So Stuff would be -- they missed Stuff and they didn't know where he was. He had gotten in a car and drove all the way back to Buffalo to see his wife.
(Laughter)
From Los Angeles.

Yeah. They said, 'Where is Stuff at?' They thought he was dead or something, you know? But he got in there -- of course the President of the Federation of that time took their cards away from them for a year, their union cards, you know? Of course they couldn't play, you know. They could play, but they -- people had come there to see Stuff Smith, so the club owner was losing money, you know? He had a case.
That was here in Los Angeles?
That's right. The club was here.
What club was that, do you know? What year was it?

Oh, it was way before I met him. Somewhere in the '30s. You know. But to hear the guys tell the story, I'm not as comical as they are. Of course I wasn't there. I'm just trying to remember bits and pieces of the story, you know? And Stuff got lonesome for his wife and

drove all the way back to Buffalo, New York. And they -- pretty soon they caught up with him, you know. But one of the reasons that John became -- he was the -- John Levy, I mean. He was the business man of the trio, because when I joined Stuff in Chicago the union wouldn't let Stuff handle the salaries. So John Levy was doing the business, with Joe Glazer at that time, you know. And when John would get sick I would do it. And Stuff would have to go to the union to get his money. Because --
For his own group?
Yeah. He was the leader. But --
(Laughter)
But he was a beautiful guy. But he had just had a breakdown when I joined him, you know. He'd been confined.
Emotionally, that kind of breakdown.
Yeah, up here in his mind, you know.
Uh-huh.

And he got out, been in a strait jacket and all that, but then he would level off and he'd be beautiful, but you know, several years or whatever. Then he would snap. But all of the time, when he was -- when he would go off or anything, he could always play beautifully.
Did it affect his music? Was his music different then?
No.
His music was consistent.

Yes, the music stayed the same. He went off but the music stayed there. And I've found a thing like that, sometimes under strain, that you'd be surprised how strong the music is, if it's deep in you, no matter what pressure you're under you can always -- sometimes it even gets better.
